requests.body:
Request changes on PR #124 (design(0003)). Re-run the design pass with the decision and the corrections below; keep intent.md unchanged.

**Decision on the open flagged concern**
1. Concern 1 (the `class` tag's vocabulary): decided. The class is free text in kebab-case; `index.py build` normalises it (lower-case; spaces and underscores to hyphens; one heading per normalised value), so a spelling drift cannot create a second heading. For an incident the weekly scan filed, the class is the `class` field of `evidence/scan-finding.json`. No controlled vocabulary now: no lesson exists to name one from (decision 17), and a list would be a guardrail edit on every project. Revisit when a project has ten lessons. Rewrite the item so it starts with "decided".

**spec.md**
2. Gate scope: the new lesson, eval and `check` sub-checks run at gate (e) only. State the guard explicitly: `ctx.status.entry_route == "incident" and ctx.phase == "e"`. Today the incident branch of `check_artifacts` sits inside the `intent.md` block, which every gate (a) to (f) runs, so without the guard every incident parks at (f) with "lesson missing" and `tests/test_gate.py::test_gate_f_waits_for_the_owner_s_triage_with_the_finding_and_its_route` turns red. Name that test as the regression guard.
3. One "what I need from you" line per failure: `check_artifacts` joins every problem into one failure with one fixed need text, so the requirement cannot be met inside that function as the Design says. Decided: a separate check `lesson_and_eval` registered at phase "e" in `CHECKS_BY_PHASE`, returning one CheckResult whose `need` lists one line per problem. Drop the "no new CHECKS_BY_PHASE entry" constraint. Add a test that asserts the rendered what-I-need text.
4. `(stale)` and a byte-exact `check` contradict each other: the day a lesson passes `stale_after`, `build` output changes with no file changed, `check` fails, and the maintain run falls back to every file until the next incident. Decided: `check` compares the index with the `(stale)` suffixes stripped from both sides, and `build`/`check` take `--today YYYY-MM-DD` for the tests. Write it under Requirements and Acceptance.
5. The glob "every `lessons/*.md`" includes `README.md` (copied into every project by `/sdlc-init`) and `index.md` itself. Exclude both by name. State that an `## Unsorted` entry (a file without a parsable frontmatter) does not fail `check`; it is listed and `check` prints a one-line note per Unsorted file. A frontmatter that does not parse is Unsorted with the parser's error in the note, never a crash.
6. Frontmatter notation: the project's YAML reader (`plugin/state/yamlish.py`) refuses flow style (`fixed: {pr: 42}` raises "flow mappings are not supported") and truncates an unquoted value at ` #`. Require block style for every nested field, and double quotes on `title` and `description`, in the README example and in step 0b. Read lesson files with `utf-8-sig` before the frontmatter split.
7. Concern 3 (Windows newline stability) was closed on a wrong basis: `yamlish.dump_file` dumps YAML and cannot write the markdown index, and a concern may be closed only by a policy or the owner, not by code. Reopen it and close it as decided by the owner with the real mechanism, stated as a requirement: the index is written with `write_text(..., newline="\n")`, `check` compares text read in universal-newline mode (a CRLF checkout must not false-positive), and every link uses `as_posix()` (the intent's forward-slash constraint, which the spec dropped).
8. `runbook` source: the "resolved route" reasoning does not hold (`Resolved.route` is always the proposal's route; `runbook_authorized_by` is set only for `go` routes). The source is `evidence/proposal.json: route` when `evidence/runbook-<name>.json` exists with `status: ran`; absent otherwise (failed or go-requested included). Make Requirements and Design say the same thing.
9. Scan-filed incidents: an incident the weekly scan files carries `evidence/scan-finding.json`, not `detection.json`; `finding.read_any` maps it to metric `security: <class>`, rule `scan`, tier 3, and there are no failed-run URLs. Add one requirement: `detected` is read through `finding.read_any`, the `detection` source points at whichever file exists, `run-<n>` sources are absent for a scan incident, and the class tag is the scan's `class` field (item 1).
10. Determinism the build would otherwise guess, write each down: the index line is `* [title](file) - description. Tier n, Mon yyyy.` (the proposal's); "newest first" sorts by `detected.at` descending, then file name; `## Unsorted` comes after `## Retired`; `build` with zero lessons writes the heading and one line "No lessons yet."; the gate finds the lesson by `lessons/*-<slug>.md` (the month varies); the required fields are every field of the table except `runbook` and `supersedes`, which are optional; "the eval case exists" means `evals/cases/<id>-<slug>/prompt.md` and `checks.yaml` both exist. Acceptance says "three sub-checks" and lists five: make the count match.
11. Restore these intent sentences the spec dropped, one Requirements bullet each: a stale lesson is still read and the maintain run says when it relied on one; `description` is one sentence in the metric's terms; a hand edit of the index is undone by the next `build`; `/sdlc-init` copies the README as today; no workflow template changes; the sample stays frozen; decision 17 unchanged.
12. Add the `supersedes` rule to the deploy requirement: when the new lesson carries `supersedes: <file>`, step 0b sets the earlier lesson's `status: retired` and adds `retired_by: <the new file>` in the same commit; the gate (e) sub-check verifies the superseded file exists and reads `retired`.
13. Both command files' `allowed-tools` frontmatter gains `Bash(python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/plugin/lessons/index.py" *)`, and the body quotes the call the same way (the instruction test requires it). CI is unaffected; a by-hand run would otherwise prompt.
14. Citations to correct: `HANDOFF.md:60-61` is item 11 (item 4 is the row at line 42); `tests/test_evals.py:701-767` are the `case.py new` CLI tests, not instruction tests; `tests/test_gate.py:2346-2364` is gate (f) coverage, not (e), and no (e) incident fixture exists yet (say to build one with `_ctx(tmp_path, phase="e")` and `entry_route="incident"`); `docs/notes/1.md`'s frontmatter is flat (`generated.at` is one key).

**plan.md**
15. Add `plugin/lessons/__init__.py` to "## Files that change" (every plugin subpackage has one; the plan-sync exemption covers `*.md` only, so step 1's commit is denied without it).
16. The "No change to …" paragraph wraps so that one line starts with `17), to \`plugin/detect/**\``, and the gate's file-list parser reads it as a numbered item: `plugin/detect/**` is currently counted as a planned file (the opposite of the sentence, and the port-list path HANDOFF tracks). Move that paragraph to Risks and make sure no continuation line in "## Files that change" starts with a digit, `-` or `*`.
17. Reflect items 2 to 13 in the file items: the phase guard and the separate check in the `checks.py` item and Risk 2; `build` excluding README and index, `--today`, the Unsorted rule, newline and `as_posix()` in the `index.py` item; the `supersedes` rule, the scan shape, block style and the `allowed-tools` line in the `sdlc-deploy.md` item; the `allowed-tools` line in the `sdlc-maintain.md` item.
18. Tests: `tests/test_lessons.py` adds README.md present and ignored, index.md ignored, malformed frontmatter to Unsorted without a crash, a CRLF index on disk passing `check`, zero lessons, the stale marker with `--today`, class normalisation; `tests/test_gate.py` adds the (e) incident fixture, the pass case, one test per failure, the rendered what-I-need text, and the (f) regression; if `artifacts.py` needs the eval case names, import them from `plugin/evals/case.py` instead of duplicating.
19. Risks: add the clock dependence of `(stale)` (item 4); fix Risk 6's fact (this repository has no root `lessons/`; only `template/lessons/README.md` exists; the conclusion stands); reword Risk 3's mitigation as instruction-text assertions in `tests/test_commands_and_skills.py` (pytest cannot assert the model's Evidence line); state that the build starts only after concern 1 is closed and that the free-text answer leaves the file list unchanged.
20. Order of work step 2 says "three new incident sub-checks"; align the count with the file item.

requests.body:
Request changes on PR #124 (design(0003)), iteration 2 of 2. Re-run the design pass with the corrections below; keep intent.md unchanged. Items 1 to 5 change what the build would do; the rest are the sentences the first review asked for and the fix round left out, plus determinism the build would otherwise guess.

**What changes the build**
1. Concern 1 and `tests/test_lessons.py` (spec.md Flagged concerns, plan.md's `test_lessons.py` item and Proof): the example `flakytest` does not follow the decided rule (lower-case; spaces and underscores to hyphens map `flakytest` to `flakytest`, not to `flaky-test`), so the planned "class normalisation" test cannot pass as written. Replace `flakytest` with `Flaky Test` in all three places.
2. Maintain from the index (spec.md Requirements, the `/sdlc-maintain` bullet; plan.md's `sdlc-maintain.md` and `index.py` items): the index line carries the title, the file, the description, the tier and the month under a heading per first tag (the class), so the metric and the runbook tags are not in the index and the maintain run cannot pick lessons "whose tags name the metric or the rule" without opening every file. Decided: every index line ends with its tags — `* [title](file) - description. Tier n, Mon yyyy. Tags: class, metric, runbook.` (the runbook omitted when there is none) — and step 1 opens the lessons whose heading or tags name `detection.json`'s metric or rule, plus `## Retired`. Write the line shape once, under the determinism bullet.
3. The rendered "what I need from you" text (spec.md Requirements and Design, the `lesson_and_eval` bullet; plan.md's `checks.py` item): `GateResult.what_i_need` prints `  - what I need: <need>` for one line, so with `need` joined by `\n` the second and later problems land at column 0, outside the bullet. Decided: `lesson_and_eval` joins the problems with `"\n    "` (a newline and four spaces), and the test asserts the whole rendered block, each problem on its own indented line.
4. The eval case's file names (plan.md's `artifacts.py` item): `plugin/evals/case.py` names `prompt.md` and `checks.yaml` as locals (`case.py:178`), not as constants, so "import them if that module already names them as constants" falls back to duplicating them, and adding constants to `case.py` would be a commit the plan-sync hook denies (it is not under "## Files that change", and Risk 1 says it does not change). Decided: the two names are constants in `plugin/gate/artifacts.py` beside the lesson's required fields, with a one-line comment naming `case.py:178` as the writer that must agree; `case.py` stays untouched. Drop the conditional.
5. The eval case in every section (spec.md Design, Acceptance; plan.md's `checks.py` and `test_gate.py` items, Order of work step 2, Risk 2, Proof): Requirements say "both `prompt.md` and `checks.yaml` exist", the other sections say "the eval case folder exists" and the fail case is "missing eval case folder". Use the Requirements meaning everywhere; the fail case is "`prompt.md` or `checks.yaml` missing".

**spec.md: the sentences the first review asked for**
6. Item 7 asked for a requirement: add one Requirements bullet stating that the index is written with `write_text(..., newline="\n")`, that `check` compares text read in universal-newline mode, and that every link is rendered with the native path's `.as_posix()` (`Path(...).as_posix()`, as `case.py:181` does; `PurePosixPath(str(p)).as_posix()` keeps a backslash from a Windows path).
7. Item 5 asked that an `## Unsorted` entry does not fail `check`: add the sentence — `check` exits 0 with `## Unsorted` entries present and prints one note line per Unsorted file; only a drift of the generated text is exit 1. Reword the README bullet's "reported by `check`" to say the same.
8. Item 4 asked for `--today` under Acceptance: add it there, with the class-normalisation test.
9. Item 9 asked that the `detection` source points at whichever file exists: in the `sources` sentence of Requirements bullet 1, say the `detection` resource is `evidence/detection.json`, or `evidence/scan-finding.json` for an incident the weekly scan filed. Replace "read through `plugin/detect/finding.read_any`" with "with the mapping `finding.read_any` implements (`finding.py:150-160`)": step 0b is instruction text for the model, nothing in the plan calls that function.
10. Item 13 asked for the `allowed-tools` lines in spec.md too: one Requirements bullet naming `Bash(python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/plugin/lessons/index.py" *)` for both command files and the body's call quoted the same way.
11. Item 11 asked for one Requirements bullet per restored sentence; they are present but folded into other bullets. Give each its own bullet.

**spec.md: determinism the build would otherwise guess**
12. Write down: the index opens with `# Lessons` and no frontmatter (nothing reads one); tag headings are ordered alphabetically by the normalised class; the link is the file name relative to `lessons/` (`(2026-10-<slug>.md)`); "Mon yyyy" is `detected.at`'s month; `description` carries no trailing period (the line adds it); an `## Unsorted` line is `* [first heading](file)` and a `## Retired` line has the tag line's shape; `(stale)` is appended at the end of the line, on `## Retired` lines too.
13. The required frontmatter fields, by name: `type`, `title`, `description`, `tags`, `change`, `detected`, `fixed`, `generated`, `status`, `stale_after`, `sources`; `runbook`, `supersedes` and `retired_by` are optional (the current sentence "every field named in the first Requirements bullet except `runbook` and `supersedes`" would make `retired_by` required on every new lesson).
14. The gate's glob: `lessons/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-<slug>.md`, so a slug that ends in another change's slug does not match; more than one match fails the check.

**plan.md**
15. Order of work step 1 names `plugin/lessons/__init__.py` (it is why the file was added).
16. `tests/test_gate.py`: one unit test calls `lesson_and_eval` with a phase (f) incident context and asserts it passes, so the guard itself is proven, not only the registration.
17. Citations: `HANDOFF.md:42` is item 2b on `main` since PR #126 (item 4 is line 39) — cite it as "HANDOFF.md, item 4" with no line; `CHECKS_BY_PHASE["e"]` is `checks.py:1646-1660`; Risk 5's "skips exactly one" is wrong (`yamlish.loads` skips every `---` before the first content line, and a `---` after content raises `expected 'key: value'`), the conclusion stands.
